publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
title: AI Agent Standards Initiative
key_claim: NIST is running a dedicated initiative, including an enterprise identity-and-authorisation project with its National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence, to build industry standards for AI agent identity because none currently exist.
frame_summary: This source is arguing that autonomous agents cannot be adopted with confidence until industry-led identity and authorisation standards exist, and that NIST's role is to catalyse those standards rather than assume enterprises already have them.
verbatim_quote: The AI Agent Standards Initiative ensures that the next generation of AI—agents capable of autonomous actions—is widely adopted with confidence.
verbatim_list: By fostering industry-led technical standards and open protocols, NIST aims to catalyze an ecosystem where agents function securely on behalf of users and interoperate smoothly across the digital landscape.
notes: Page shows 'Created February 17, 2026, Updated August 14, 2026'; the initiative's identity and authorisation strand is a live NCCoE project still at the concept-paper stage as of this scan.

title: New Cloud Security Alliance Survey Reveals 82% of Enterprises Have Unknown AI Agents in Their Environments
key_claim: A survey of 418 IT and security professionals found 82% of organisations have unknown AI agents running in their infrastructure, 68% nonetheless believe they have strong visibility, and only 21% have a formal decommissioning process.
frame_summary: This source is arguing that AI agent deployment has outrun enterprise inventory and lifecycle discipline, and that organisational confidence in visibility is itself unreliable, not just the underlying agent population.
verbatim_quote: found that nearly all organizations (82%) have unknown AI agents running in the IT infrastructure
verbatim_list: with only 21% of respondents having formal decommissioning processes in place
notes: Survey conducted online by CSA in January 2026, 418 respondents; commissioned by Token Security, CSA performed the analysis. Used as the one structural anchor (published 21/04/2026, within the 3-6 month band) because it is the primary quantitative base for the governance-gap framing. Vendor-commissioned, so treat_directionally is set even though CSA disclosed methodology and sample size.

title: Agents are now on the org chart. Who is managing them?
key_claim: One major software company already runs roughly 3,000 AI agents against its human headcount, a 3:1 ratio, and KPMG proposes splitting the Chief AI Officer role into a Platform CAIO reporting to the CTO and a Strategy CAIO for workforce and governance reporting to the chief executive.
frame_summary: This source is arguing that AI agents are already being organised like a second workforce inside leading firms, and that CHROs, not just CIOs, should own the governance and workforce dimension of that population before the ownership question is settled by default.
verbatim_quote: roughly three thousand AI agents - a 3:1 ratio of agents to employees
verbatim_list: the Platform CAIO, focused on data, infrastructure, and engineering, reporting to the CTO; and the Strategy CAIO, focused on business value, governance, and workforce, reporting to the chief executive
notes: The 3:1 ratio describes one named major software company, not a cross-enterprise average; used in the article as an outlier data point and named as such, and revisited in the Counter-Argument section.

title: Technology Spotlight - Accounting for AI Costs Associated With Internal-Use Software Development
key_claim: Existing internal-use software accounting rules apply unchanged to AI agents doing development work, and costs cannot be allocated to projects on the basis of developer headcount or similar proxies; each cost must be directly attributable to a qualifying project.
frame_summary: This source is arguing that agent-related costs need the same project-level attribution discipline as any other development cost, and explicitly warns against using headcount as a shortcut, which removes the easiest way finance teams might otherwise count agents as workforce.
verbatim_quote: The internal-use software accounting framework does not change merely because the development resource is an AI-enabled service rather than a person.
verbatim_list: Allocating the cost of a broadly available AI tool to software projects on the basis of developer headcount, labor hours, broad project budgets, or similar measures does not, in and of itself, establish that the cost is related to materials or services directly consumed by those projects.
notes: Deloitte's internal technical accounting guidance (DART), addressed to preparers; scoped to internal-use software development costs rather than to broader agent workforce classification.

publisher: SSRN (University of Illinois / Northeastern University / University of Florida working paper)
title: Boundary Design in Agentic Organizations
date_evidence: Date Written: August 26, 2026 (54 Pages Posted: 10 Sep 2026)
key_claim: Organisations deploying employee-customised AI agents face a governance choice over how openly those agents' capabilities can be shared across the organisation, and the authors describe this as a new layer of organisational governance introduced by agentic AI.
frame_summary: This source is arguing that agent deployment creates a genuinely new organisational-design problem, not just a security or IT-provisioning one, because how freely an agent's capabilities circulate changes employee incentives to build them in the first place.
verbatim_quote: organizations must govern not only what AI agents can do, but also how freely the capabilities they carry can move across the organization
notes: Working paper by Yangguang Wang (Illinois, Gies College of Business), Guohou Shan (Northeastern, D'Amore-McKim) and Liangfei Qiu (Florida, Warrington College). Not yet peer-reviewed; cited as Tier 2 academic working paper on a recognised repository per tier-rubric.

title: Shadow agents: How IT leaders must govern 'headless' AI before it breaks the enterprise
date_evidence: By Sunil Gentyala, Contributor -- Jul 1, 2026 -- 8 mins read
key_claim: Shadow AI agents deployed outside IT's sanctioned tooling are already running in production, summarising documents, routing decisions and interacting with systems that monitoring tools cannot observe, and accountability for governing them is defaulting to IT leaders.
frame_summary: This source is arguing that shadow agents are a present operational reality rather than a future risk, and that IT leadership, not any other function, is the party being asked to build accountability infrastructure around them.
verbatim_quote: Shadow agents are not a future problem. They are in production today, summarizing documents, routing decisions and interacting with systems your monitoring tools cannot observe.
notes: Byline: Sunil Gentyala, Contributor. Article frames accountability exclusively as an IT/security responsibility, with no mention of HR or workforce-planning involvement, which is itself evidence for this scan's framing.

title: Gartner Unveils Top Strategic Predictions for 2027 and Beyond
key_claim: By 2030, 80% of Global 500 companies will contractually make their CIO or CAIO the 'Evidence Custodian' for AI accountability.
frame_summary: This source is arguing that AI accountability is heading toward a formal, contractual designation sitting with a technology executive, and treats that as the emerging default answer to who is responsible when an autonomous system acts.
verbatim_quote: By 2030, 80% of Global 500 companies will contractually make their CIO (or CAIO) the 'Evidence Custodian' for AI accountability.
notes: Analyst-firm press release; predictive methodology not disclosed on the page, so tiered as Tier 4 vendor/analyst forecast per tier-rubric's explicit Gartner-press example, used only as directional corroboration of where accountability is heading, not as an anchor for a current-state claim. Title's '2027' names the horizon of the predictions themselves (Gartner's annual 'Top Strategic Predictions for [next year] and Beyond' series); this is the original 15/09/2026 release, not a stale prior edition, confirmed by the dateline and by the 2030-dated Evidence Custodian prediction cited in this scan.
